newsitem.title: JAPAN: Crudes slip in Asia, Dubai premiums looking up.
newsitem.headline: Crudes slip in Asia, Dubai premiums looking up.

text.p: Crude oil prices slipped on Tuesday in late Asian trading, continuing a three-day downtrend in a market marked by an absence of fresh trading incentives, market participants said.
At 0730 GMT, January cash Brent was notionally assessed at $22.70/22.80, down 15 cents from late Monday U.S. levels.
On SIMEX, January Brent was most recently traded at $22.80.
A January/February Dubai spread was reported done at 49 cents once and 50 cents twice. The seller in all three cases was reported to be a trader. A March/April Dubai was believed traded at 45 cents.
Paper Tapis for January was assessed at $23.40/23.60 per barrel.

In the wet market, light-grade Gulf crudes were firm but the high offers indicated appear to have prompted many potential buyers to adopt a wait-and-see stance and there were few firm bids placed in the market.

January Dubai was reported done at the same or higher levels than last week. A U.S. major was believed to have purchased two January Dubai cargoes at 65 cents and 67 cents, respectively, compared with 65 cents last week. There was also market talk of a January Dubai done at a mid-70 cent premium.
January Lower Zakum was discussed both sides of ADNOC plus 65 cents. Some traders said January Umm Shaif was fetching a premium of about 75 cents above the official selling price.
An unconfirmed report was heard of a January Oman done at MPM plus 12 cents.

In regional crudes, a 200,000-barrel December Lalang was rumoured to have been sold to a Japanese refiner at ICP plus 40 cents. A December Kutubu was believed to be on offer for a premium of 35 cents above the official selling price.
